start.text: Good evening. Do you have a table for one?

choices.text: Good evening! Yes, right this way. Here is the menu.
choices.tip: Polite greeting! Repeating the customer's greeting ('Good evening') and using 'right this way' sounds professional and welcoming.

choices.text: Yeah, just sit anywhere.
choices.tip: Too casual. 'Yeah' and 'just sit anywhere' sound careless. Try: 'Yes, of course. Please follow me.'

menu.text: Thank you. I'm quite hungry, but I'm not very familiar with Japanese food. What do you recommend?

choices.text: Our Salmon Nigiri Set is very popular. It's fresh and delicious.
choices.tip: Great recommendation! Use 'popular' and two adjectives ('fresh and delicious') to make food sound attractive.

choices.text: The Ikura Gunkan is a chef's favourite. It's rich and a little salty.
choices.tip: Nice! 'A chef's favourite' makes the dish sound special. Describing taste ('rich', 'a little salty') helps the customer decide.

choices.text: Before I recommend something, is there anything you don't eat?
choices.tip: Excellent service! Asking about food the customer doesn't eat is polite and shows you care. 'Is there anything you don't eat?' is a very useful question.

choices.text: I don't know, everything is good. Just pick something.
choices.tip: Unhelpful. The customer asked for advice. 'I don't know' and 'just pick something' sound lazy. Try: 'I'd recommend…'

vocab.meaning: knowing something well because you have seen or used it before
to suggest something because you think it is good

recommend_salmon.text: That sounds great! I love salmon. Does the set come with anything else?

choices.text: Yes, it includes a bowl of hot miso soup and a small salad.
choices.tip: Clear answer! 'It includes…' is a useful phrase to explain what comes with a set meal.

choices.text: No. Just the sushi.
choices.tip: Too short. A one-word 'No' sounds cold. Try: 'It comes with miso soup. Would you like to add a salad?'

vocab.meaning: a meal with several dishes served together for one price

drink.text: Perfect. Could I also get something to drink?

choices.text: Of course! Would you prefer hot green tea or cold water?
choices.tip: Great! 'Would you prefer A or B?' is a polite way to offer choices and helps the customer decide quickly.

choices.text: The drinks are in the fridge. Get it yourself.
choices.tip: Rude! Customers expect you to serve them. Try: 'Of course. What would you like to drink?'

recommend_ikura.text: Ikura? I've never heard of it. What is it exactly?

choices.text: It's salmon roe. They're small orange fish eggs that pop in your mouth.
choices.tip: Very clear! Explaining a new food with simple words, colour and texture ('small', 'orange', 'pop') makes it easy to understand.

choices.text: Fish eggs. Do you want it or not?
choices.tip: Impatient. 'Do you want it or not?' sounds pushy. Try: 'It's salmon roe. Would you like to try it?'

vocab.meaning: used to ask for more detail or a clear answer

ikura_reply.text: Interesting! I'd like to try something new. I'll have the Ikura Gunkan, please.

choices.text: Excellent choice. Coming right up!
choices.tip: 'Excellent choice' compliments the customer, and 'Coming right up!' is a friendly way to say the food will be ready soon.

vocab.meaning: to do or eat something for the first time

order_confirmed_ikura.text: I can't wait to try it!

ask_diet.text: Thank you for asking! Actually, I'm vegetarian, so I don't eat fish or meat.

choices.text: No problem! Our Avocado Cucumber Roll has no fish at all. It's fresh and crunchy.
choices.tip: Perfect! 'No problem!' makes the customer feel comfortable, and you offered a suitable dish right away.

choices.text: Sushi without fish? That's a bit strange.
choices.tip: Impolite. Never judge a customer's diet. Respect their choice and help: 'Of course. We have a vegetable roll.'

vocab.meaning: a person who does not eat meat or fish

veggie_happy.text: Wonderful! That sounds delicious. I'll have the Avocado Cucumber Roll.

choices.text: Great choice. I'll make sure there's no fish in it.
choices.tip: Good! Repeating the customer's request ('no fish') shows you listened carefully.

veggie_upset.text: It's not strange, it's my choice. Do you have anything without fish or not?

choices.text: I'm sorry, that was rude of me. We have an Avocado Cucumber Roll.
choices.tip: Good recovery! A sincere apology ('I'm sorry, that was rude of me') can fix a mistake. Then offer a solution.

choices.text: Fine. There's a vegetable roll.
choices.tip: Still unfriendly. 'Fine.' sounds annoyed. Apologise first, then offer the dish politely.

order_confirmed_veggie.text: Thank you. I'm looking forward to it.

vocab.meaning: feeling happy and excited about something that will happen

recommend_bad.text: Oh... well, I guess I'll just have the Tuna Nigiri then.

choices.text: Tuna it is. I'll get that for you.
choices.tip: This is OK, but the customer is already disappointed. Adding an apology helps: 'Sorry about that. Tuna is a great choice.'

wasabi.text: Is the green paste spicy? I'm not good with spicy food.

choices.text: Yes, that's wasabi. I can leave it out for you if you like.
choices.tip: Very helpful! 'I can leave it out' offers to change the dish. 'If you like' makes the offer polite.

choices.text: It's not that spicy. You'll be fine.
choices.tip: Ignoring the customer's concern is not good service. Offer to change the dish: 'I can make it without wasabi.'

vocab.meaning: a soft, thick mixture
having a hot, strong taste that burns your mouth a little

order_confirmed_tuna_plain.text: Thank you, that's very kind. No wasabi, please!

vocab.meaning: friendly and helpful

order_confirmed_salmon.text: I'm looking forward to the meal!

vocab.meaning: feeling happy and excited about something that will happen

order_confirmed_tuna.text: Please don't take too long, I'm in a hurry.

vocab.meaning: needing to do something quickly because you don't have much time

ikura_bad.text: Hmm, that doesn't sound very nice. I'll just have a Salmon Roll instead.

choices.text: Of course. Sorry, I should have explained it better.
choices.tip: Good recovery! 'I should have…' is a polite way to admit a mistake.

choices.text: OK.
choices.tip: Acceptable, but very short. Add something friendly: 'Of course. A Salmon Roll coming right up!'

vocab.meaning: in place of something else

order_confirmed_salmon_roll.text: Thanks. Please don't make me wait too long.

start.text: Ciao! It smells amazing in here. I am absolutely famished!

choices.text: Welcome to Bella Trattoria! Can I start you off with some drinks?
choices.tip: Perfect! 'Can I start you off with…?' is a polite, natural way to offer drinks first.

choices.text: Are you ready to order or do you need a minute?
choices.tip: This sounds rushed. The customer just sat down. Give them time and welcome them first.

vocab.meaning: extremely hungry

drinks.text: Just sparkling water with lemon, please. What is your signature dish?

choices.text: Our classic wood-fired Margherita Pizza is a favourite: tomato, mozzarella and fresh basil.
choices.tip: Great! Naming the main ingredients helps the customer imagine the dish.

choices.text: If you like mushrooms, our Mushroom Pizza is very popular.
choices.tip: Nice! 'If you like…' is a friendly way to suggest something that matches the customer's taste.

choices.text: Pizza is pizza. Just pick one.
choices.tip: Rude. The customer asked for your advice. Try: 'I'd recommend our Margherita.'

vocab.meaning: the special dish a restaurant is most famous for

rushing.text: I just sat down! But fine, I will just take a Margherita Pizza.

choices.text: Sorry to rush you. One Margherita Pizza coming right up.
choices.tip: Good recovery! Saying sorry quickly fixes the mistake.

choices.text: Yes, it is. There's no meat in it at all.
choices.tip: Clear and confident. 'No meat at all' answers the question completely.

choices.text: Probably.
choices.tip: Not sure is not good enough when a customer asks about food. Check, then answer clearly.

vocab.meaning: without any meat or fish

funghi.text: I love mushrooms! Are they fresh?

choices.text: Yes, we get fresh mushrooms from the market every morning.
choices.tip: Excellent! A detail like 'from the market every morning' makes your answer believable.

choices.text: They come from a can.
choices.tip: Honest, but it doesn't sell the dish. Focus on something good: 'They're cooked with garlic and herbs.'

vocab.meaning: recently picked or made, not old

bad.text: Oh... all right. A Margherita, then.

choices.text: Sorry about that. A Margherita it is!
choices.tip: Good recovery! A short apology and a cheerful confirmation.

choices.text: OK.
choices.tip: Acceptable, but an apology would help after being rude.

crispy_margherita.text: Perfetto! Please make sure the crust is nice and crispy.

vocab.meaning: the hard outside edge of a pizza or bread
hard and dry in a pleasant way, making a sound when you bite it

crispy_funghi.text: Perfetto! Please make sure the crust is nice and crispy.

vocab.meaning: the hard outside edge of a pizza or bread
hard and dry in a pleasant way, making a sound when you bite it

start.text: Sawasdee krub! I need something really flavorful and spicy today.

choices.text: Sawasdee! You've come to the right place. How about our Som Tam Poo?
choices.tip: Great! A friendly greeting plus a clear suggestion.

choices.text: Everything here is spicy. What do you want?
choices.tip: Too blunt. Help the customer choose: 'How about our Som Tam?'

vocab.meaning: having a strong, delicious taste

recommend.text: Som Tam Poo? What does it taste like?

choices.text: It's a papaya salad with salted crab. It's salty, sour and spicy.
choices.tip: Excellent! Describing the taste with 'salty, sour and spicy' helps the customer imagine the dish.

choices.text: It's just salad.
choices.tip: Too short. Tell the customer the main ingredients and how it tastes.

vocab.meaning: what flavour something has

rude_start.text: Uh... okay. Just give me a Som Tam Poo, extra spicy I guess.

choices.text: Sorry about that. Coming right up! How many chilies would you like?
choices.tip: Good recovery! Apologise, then ask a useful question.

choices.text: Sure, whatever.
choices.tip: Still unfriendly. Try: 'Sure! How spicy would you like it?'

spice.text: I love it spicy. How many chilies do you usually put in?

choices.text: One chili is mild. For Thai spicy, I use three chilies.
choices.tip: Perfect! Using numbers ('one chili', 'three chilies') makes the spice level clear.

choices.text: I don't count. I just throw some in.
choices.tip: Unclear. The customer can't choose if you don't explain. Give numbers.

vocab.meaning: small hot peppers that make food spicy

confirm.text: Three chilies, please. Thai spicy! I love it when it burns a little.

vocab.meaning: very spicy, the way many Thai people like it
gives a hot, painful feeling (here: from spicy food)

start.text: Bonjour! Such a charming café. Do you have any seasonal pastries today?

choices.text: Bonjour! Yes, our Berry Macaron Tower is perfect for this season.
choices.tip: Lovely! You answered the question ('Yes') and gave a specific recommendation with a reason ('perfect for this season').

choices.text: We just have what's in the display case.
choices.tip: This is unhelpful. Even if the choice is limited, describe something: 'Today we have…'

vocab.meaning: pleasant and attractive
available only at a particular time of year
sweet baked foods such as croissants or tarts

recommend_macaron.text: A Berry Macaron Tower? Oh, that sounds simply divine! Is it very sweet?

choices.text: It has a perfect balance of sweetness from the macarons and tartness from fresh berries.
choices.tip: Excellent description! 'A perfect balance of A and B' is an advanced way to describe flavour.

choices.text: Yes, it's sugar basically.
choices.tip: 'Basically sugar' sounds negative and lazy. Describe the taste politely: 'It's quite sweet, but…'

vocab.meaning: extremely good or delicious (informal)

rude_start.text: Oh... I see. I suppose I'll just take the Macaron Tower then.

choices.text: Right away. I'll make sure it's plated beautifully.
choices.tip: Good! 'Right away' plus a promise ('I'll make sure…') shows care and builds trust.

choices.text: Okay.
choices.tip: A one-word answer like 'Okay.' can feel cold. Add a little more: 'Of course, I'll bring it right away.'

order_macaron.text: Wonderful. I'll have an Earl Grey tea to pair with it, please.

vocab.meaning: to serve one food or drink together with another because they go well together

order_macaron_bad.text: I hope it's at least edible.

vocab.meaning: safe or good enough to eat

start.text: Hey there! I'm starved. Got any good burgers?

choices.text: You bet! Our Classic Cheeseburger is the best in town.
choices.tip: Great energy! 'You bet!' is informal but friendly, which matches this casual diner. 'Best in town' is a confident recommendation.

choices.text: Yeah, burgers are on the menu.
choices.tip: Correct but flat. The customer is excited; answer with energy and recommend something specific.

vocab.meaning: very hungry (informal)

recommend_burger.text: Awesome! Load it up with a beef patty and lots of cheese.

choices.text: Coming right up, hot and fresh off the grill!
choices.tip: Energetic and friendly. 'Fresh off the grill' makes the burger sound delicious.

rude_start.text: Alright, alright. I'll just take a Classic Cheeseburger.

choices.text: Sure thing. Give me a minute.
choices.tip: OK, but a little flat. A warmer reply: 'Great choice! Coming right up.'

order_burger.text: Can't wait! My stomach is rumbling.

vocab.meaning: making a low, continuous sound, like an empty stomach

hold.text: Oh, and could you hold the lettuce? I'm not a fan.

choices.text: Sure thing! One cheeseburger, no lettuce.
choices.tip: Perfect! You repeated the change to the order so there's no mistake.

choices.text: Lettuce is healthy, you know.
choices.tip: Don't argue with the customer. Just say: 'No problem, no lettuce.'

vocab.meaning: don't put lettuce on it
don't like something very much

order_burger_no_lettuce.text: Can't wait! My stomach is rumbling.

vocab.meaning: making a long, low sound (a hungry stomach)

start.text: Hi! Sorry, I'm in a bit of a rush. How long does a sushi roll take?

choices.text: Hello! A roll takes about five minutes. Would you like one?
choices.tip: Great! Answer the question first with a clear time ('about five minutes'), then make an offer: 'Would you like one?'

choices.text: It depends. Why are you in a rush?
choices.tip: Too personal. The customer didn't ask for a chat. Just tell them the time: 'It takes about five minutes.'

vocab.meaning: a little busy and needing to do things quickly

menu.text: Five minutes is perfect. Which one do you recommend?

choices.text: The Salmon Roll is our best seller. It's fresh and simple.
choices.tip: Nice! 'Best seller' means many people buy it. It's a strong reason to choose a dish.

choices.text: The Tuna Nigiri is quick to make and very fresh today.
choices.tip: Good thinking! The customer is in a rush, so 'quick to make' answers what she really needs.

choices.text: Whatever. They're all the same.
choices.tip: Rude and unhelpful. 'Whatever' sounds like you don't care. Try: 'I'd recommend the Salmon Roll.'

vocab.meaning: to suggest something because you think it is good

salmon_side.text: Great, a Salmon Roll then. Could I have extra soy sauce on the side?

choices.text: Of course. I'll put some soy sauce on the side for you.
choices.tip: Perfect! Repeating the request ('soy sauce on the side') shows you listened.

choices.text: Soy sauce is already on the table.
choices.tip: Not wrong, but a bit cold. Friendlier: 'Sure! There's some on the table, and I can bring you more.'

vocab.meaning: served separately, not on top of the food

tuna_side.text: Sounds good. Is the tuna fresh today?

choices.text: Yes, it arrived this morning. It's very fresh.
choices.tip: Excellent! Giving a fact ('it arrived this morning') makes your answer believable.

choices.text: I think so.
choices.tip: Unsure answers worry customers. If you know, say it clearly: 'Yes, it's very fresh.'

vocab.meaning: recently made, caught or picked, not old

bad.text: Oh... OK. Then just a Salmon Roll, please. Quickly.

choices.text: Sorry about that. One Salmon Roll, coming right up!
choices.tip: Good recovery! A quick apology and 'coming right up' show you'll be fast.

choices.text: Fine.
choices.tip: Still unfriendly. Apologise first: 'Sorry about that. I'll make it quickly.'

start.text: Good evening, young man. Could you speak a little slowly, please? My hearing isn't very good.

choices.text: Of course. Good evening. Please take your time.
choices.tip: Kind and clear! Short, simple sentences are easier to hear. 'Please take your time' is very polite.

choices.text: WHAT WOULD YOU LIKE?!
choices.tip: Shouting sounds rude. Speak slowly and clearly, not loudly.

vocab.meaning: the ability to hear sounds

menu.text: Thank you, dear. I'd like something soft. My teeth aren't very strong.

choices.text: Would you like the Ikura Gunkan? The salmon roe is soft and easy to eat.
choices.tip: Great! You listened to her need ('soft') and explained why the dish fits: 'easy to eat'.

choices.text: The Tuna Nigiri is very soft and tender.
choices.tip: Good! 'Tender' is a useful word for food that is soft and easy to bite.

choices.text: Sushi is all the same. Just eat it.
choices.tip: Very rude. Never tell a customer 'just eat it'. Help them choose: 'This one is soft.'

vocab.meaning: not hard; easy to press or bite

ikura.text: That sounds lovely. Is it very salty?

choices.text: Just a little. Would you like some green tea with it?
choices.tip: Nice! You answered and then offered something extra. Green tea goes well with salty food.

choices.text: Yes. Very salty.
choices.tip: True, but very short. Add something helpful: 'A little. Green tea goes well with it.'

vocab.meaning: tasting of salt

tuna.text: Lovely. Could you make it without wasabi, please? It's too strong for me.

choices.text: Certainly. I'll make it without wasabi.
choices.tip: Perfect! 'Certainly' is a very polite 'yes', and you repeated her request.

choices.text: But wasabi is good for you.
choices.tip: Don't argue with a customer's request. Say: 'Certainly. No wasabi for you.'

vocab.meaning: having more taste than someone likes

bad.text: Oh dear. Then I'll have the Salmon Nigiri, I suppose.

choices.text: I'm sorry, madam. One Salmon Nigiri for you.
choices.tip: Good recovery! 'Madam' is a polite way to speak to an older woman.

choices.text: OK.
choices.tip: Acceptable, but an apology would help after being rude.

vocab.meaning: said when you agree but are not very happy about it
friendly and caring

start.text: Good evening, young man. Is the pasta fresh here?

choices.text: Good evening! Yes, we make it fresh every morning.
choices.tip: Great! A polite greeting plus a clear fact.

choices.text: It's from a packet, like everywhere.
choices.tip: This makes the food sound cheap. If you can, say something positive about it.

vocab.meaning: recently made, not old

menu.text: Wonderful. I'd like spaghetti, but nothing too spicy, please. And I like my pasta al dente.

choices.text: Our Spaghetti Pomodoro has a mild tomato sauce. It isn't spicy at all.
choices.tip: Perfect! 'Mild' is the opposite of 'spicy', and you showed you listened.

choices.text: You should try our chilli spaghetti. It's the best!
choices.tip: You didn't listen. She said 'nothing too spicy'. Always match your suggestion to the request.

vocab.meaning: having a hot, burning taste
cooked so it is still a little firm when you bite it

not_listening.text: I just said nothing spicy, young man.

choices.text: I'm sorry. Then I'd suggest the Spaghetti Pomodoro. It's mild.
choices.tip: Good recovery! Apologise, then give a suggestion that fits.

choices.text: Fine, the normal one, then.
choices.tip: It works, but it sounds annoyed. Add 'I'm sorry' first.

cheese.text: That sounds perfect. Could I have some extra cheese on top?

choices.text: Certainly. I'll add some grated Parmesan on top.
choices.tip: Excellent! 'Certainly' is a polite yes, and you repeated her request clearly.

choices.text: Cheese costs extra.
choices.tip: Talking about money first sounds unfriendly, and now she won't get her cheese. Say yes, then mention the price politely if needed.

vocab.meaning: placed on the highest part of something
friendly and caring

confirm_plain.text: Oh. Never mind the cheese, then.

vocab.meaning: said when you decide something is not important any more

start.text: Hi! Before I order, I should tell you: I'm allergic to peanuts.

choices.text: Thank you for telling me. I'll make your som tam without peanuts.
choices.tip: Excellent! Thank the customer and confirm you can help. Allergies are serious.

choices.text: Just pick them out if you see any.
choices.tip: Dangerous and rude. Even a small amount can make someone very sick. Leave the allergen out completely.

vocab.meaning: having a bad reaction to something you eat or touch

menu.text: Thanks. I'd like the Som Tam Thai, the sweet and sour one.

choices.text: Great choice. It has dried shrimp, tomatoes and palm sugar.
choices.tip: Nice! Naming the ingredients helps her check the dish is safe for her.

choices.text: OK. Peanuts are the best part, though.
choices.tip: Insensitive. She just told you she's allergic. Never push an allergen.

vocab.meaning: tasting of sugar and of something like lime at the same time

spice.text: How spicy is it? I can't eat very spicy food.

choices.text: I can make it mild with just one chili.
choices.tip: Clear answer! 'Mild' and 'one chili' tell her exactly what to expect.

choices.text: Thai food is always spicy.
choices.tip: Not helpful, and not true. Offer a choice: 'I can make it mild.'

vocab.meaning: having a hot, burning taste

confirm.text: One chili and no peanuts, please. Thank you!

start.text: Good morning! Are you still serving breakfast?

choices.text: Good morning! Yes, we serve breakfast until eleven.
choices.tip: Clear and friendly. Giving the time ('until eleven') answers the question fully.

choices.text: It's almost eleven. Hurry up.
choices.tip: Rude. Never rush a customer. Just tell them the time politely.

vocab.meaning: the first meal of the day

menu.text: Great! I'd love something fluffy and sweet.

choices.text: Our pancakes are light and fluffy. They come with butter and maple syrup.
choices.tip: Great description! 'Light and fluffy' matches exactly what she asked for.

choices.text: We have pancakes. They're fine.
choices.tip: 'They're fine' doesn't make anyone hungry. Describe the food: 'light and fluffy'.

vocab.meaning: soft and light, full of air

fruit.text: Pancakes, yes please! Which fruit would you recommend on top?

choices.text: The strawberries are very fresh this week.
choices.tip: Nice! 'This week' tells her the fruit is special right now.

choices.text: Blueberries go really well with maple syrup.
choices.tip: Good! 'Go well with' means two foods taste good together.

vocab.meaning: placed on the highest part of something

confirm_straw.text: Strawberries it is! Thank you so much.

confirm_blue.text: Mmm, blueberries! Thank you so much.

start.text: Howdy! Just a side of fries for me. How long will that take?

choices.text: About five minutes. We cut them fresh.
choices.tip: Great! A clear time plus a reason the food is good ('we cut them fresh').

choices.text: As long as it takes.
choices.tip: Unclear and a bit rude. Give a time: 'About five minutes.'

vocab.meaning: a small extra dish served with a meal

salt.text: Sounds good. Could you go easy on the salt? Doctor's orders.

choices.text: No problem. I'll leave the salt off, and you can add your own.
choices.tip: Perfect! You followed his request and gave him a choice.

choices.text: Fries need salt, trust me.
choices.tip: Don't argue, especially about health. Say: 'No problem, no salt.'

vocab.meaning: use only a little of something
thanked; you are grateful for it
